DCX STRATEGY 49 Construction began on the DARHT Facility in 1994. The project included two advanced LIAs that provided signifi- cantly improved diagnostics and reliability compared to previous radiographic hydrodynamic testing facilities. Novel AXIS 1 AXIS 2 mission-enhancing capabilities, such as rapid time-resolved imaging capturing three-dimensional information, were realized with the construction of Axis 2. The first hydrotest was fired at DARHT in 2000. Use of high- strength, spherical steel vessels to fully contain hydrotests was subsequently realized. Today, all DARHT tests are conducted in contain- ment vessels, allowing NNSA and LANL to meet the requirements of the DARHT Environmental Impact Study Record of Decision, simultaneously reducing emissions, enhancing safety, and enabling precision fielding of enhanced diagnostics and radiography. Advancements to the DARHT Facility have been realized throughout its service life, such as the Weather Enclosure (WE) addition that took advantage of DARHT's use of confinement vessels by enclosing the firing point, providing year-round indoor operations, and greatly enhancing operational cadence and safety. 50 DCX STRATEGY DCX Summary Over the past 25 years, DARHT has expanded from a single-axis, single- pulse, outdoor radiographic facility to a dual-axis, multi-pulse, indoor, vessel confined, radiographic facility that provides essential data for weapon designers. A senior weapon designer once stated they were addicted as soon as they saw their first radiograph from DARHT. With this amazing capability growth, DARHT has proven to be extremely reliable and has successfully collected high-quality data from every dynamic and static experiment brought to the facility for execution. In addition, the two decades of accelerator use (spanning more than 73,000 combined LIA shots) were enabled by continuous machine monitoring, careful operations, maintenance, and addressing of design issues as they were identified.
